{"success": true, "doc_name": "ILPA__ILPA_Due_Diligence_Questionnaire_v1.2.pdf", "structure": [{"title": "Preface", "node_id": "0000", "start_index": 1, "end_index": 3, "summary": "The document’s contents include an overview, FAQs, cover sheet, basic and detailed questions, and appendices for requested documents and templates covering team members, references, funds, and portfolio investments. Version 1.1 (September 2016) added ILPA Reporting Template questions, revised governance and risk/compliance/ESG content to align with PRI guidance, and refreshed links and formatting. Version 1.2 (September 2018) added Diversity and Inclusion questions, six Appendix A documents including a Team Diversity Template, and clarified Detailed Question 4.4; a red-line version is available at ilpa.org. The ILPA DDQ was developed with industry participants to reduce redundant, customized diligence questionnaires and administrative burden while supporting transparency and analysis. Compiled from more than a dozen questionnaires and reviewed by an ILPA committee and industry leaders, it is voluntary and does not replace LP-specific diligence. Its 14 topics span firm and fund information, strategy, process, team, alignment, markets, terms, governance/risk/compliance, ESG, track record, accounting/reporting, legal/administration, and diversity/inclusion. It provides short- and long-form questions and suggested diligence documents/data. A confidentiality and limitations disclaimer, ILPA contact details, and directions for further information are included."}, {"title": "Frequently Asked Questions", "node_id": "0001", "start_index": 4, "end_index": 5, "summary": "The ILPA DDQ aims to reduce diligence workload and redundant customized questionnaires, but its use is voluntary and may not suit every fund. GPs may focus firm-level answers on business units relevant to the fund, while briefly describing unrelated units and explaining exclusions. Sensitive information need not be disclosed where confidentiality or other concerns apply; GPs may offer it in person, redacted, or later, with an explanation and guidance. GPs should answer relevant questions and explain skipped detailed questions briefly; mark skipped basic questions “N/A” in the Reference field. Basic yes/no answers are a checklist, not investment criteria by themselves: LPs should review detailed responses and follow up. Additional questions should be provided separately, not added to the DDQ. “Team Members” includes firm personnel and specified former personnel; “Principals” are management and other core contributors, designated at GP discretion with rationale available. Answers should be included in the DDQ rather than merely cited from the PPM."}, {"title": "Cover Sheet", "node_id": "0002", "start_index": 6, "end_index": 6, "summary": "A cover sheet collecting general firm and fund information.
